**Method 1**

When we multiply a complex number and its conjugate, the result is always the sum of squares of the real part and the imaginary part.

For the given complex number $z=-3-8\text{i},$ the real part is $\text{Re}(z)=-3,$ and the imaginary part is $\text{Im}(z)=-8,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z\overset{―}{z} & =(\text{Re}(z))^{2}+(\text{Im}(z))^{2} \\  & =(-3)^{2}+(-8)^{2} \\  & =9+64 \\  & =73.\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

Alternatively, we can actually carry out the process of multiplying the complex number and its conjugate.

To obtain the conjugate of the complex number $z=-3-8\text{i},$ we flip the sign of the imaginary part and get $\overset{―}{z}=-3+8\text{i}.$

Multiplying, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z\overset{―}{z} & =(-3-8\text{i})(-3+8\text{i}) \\  & =(3)^{2}+(-3)(8)\text{i}+(-8)(-3)\text{i}-{\text{i}}^{2}(8)^{2} \\  & =9-\cancel{24\text{i}}+\cancel{24\text{i}}-(-1)(64) \\  & =9+64 \\  & =73.\end{aligned}
$$
